If the gun isn't well suited for the job, you may have to compensate with ammo that is more suited for the job. Finding a heavy, slower, hollow point bullet that can be quickly (and reliably) fed into the gun in a manner that permits as close to 10 accessible shots will be the key.

Going by that, you'd want a 'smaller' bolt-action rifle with a relatively 'shorter' barrel, like 16"-20" or so. You'd also want a gun with either a detachable box mag or one that can be fed 5+ round stripper clips. The next thing you'd really need is the heaviest, slowest hollow point ammo you can reasonably obtain. The idea is to make your "home defense bolt-action rifle" as close to the next best alternative (high-capacity semi-auto carbine) as you can, and the ammo choice is to lower risk of over-penetration while maintaining effective use of the bullet itself.

For a cheapo, one could get a mosin carbine/paratrooper model with a shorter barrel and keep access to some stripper clips loaded with 150+ gr, soft point ammo. Resist the urge to affix bayonet.

For someone with a little bit more wealth to shop around with, a Ruger Gunsite scout rifle covers all these points. They can be had in .308, 5.56mm, and even .450 Bushmaster now. They also come with a 10-round detachable box mag, that you could keep loaded up with some decent close-range hollow point ammo.

Bolt action for home defense is not highly recommended. Home defense ranges are about a maximum of 7 yards (21 feet). You will want more than one shot, and re-chambering a round under incredible stress and adrenaline at a distance of five yards is a serious problem.

Everyone has their own opinion, but the best home defense weapons are probably pump shotguns and gas operated / auto loading rifles. Specifically, auto loading rifles chambered in .223 / 5.56. Each can be addressed separately. You would want to base your decision upon who else is in your house, how close are your nearest neighbors, and what direction(s) would you realistically be firing upon an intruder. We can take a moment to discuss both intermediate caliber auto-loading rifles and shotguns separately:

Auto-loading Rifles Most full power hunting calibers of rifle (308, 30-06 etc) are going to have far too much penetration to be used adequately in a home defense situation. Even the 762 x39 from an AK / SKS will have too much penetration. You want something that is going to rip apart in the walls and impart its force upon the target very quickly. The best round for this is the .223 / 5.56. Mini-14s and AR15s are the best way to go. They will typically go through about 4 sheets of drywall before stopping, which means the rounds you fire will probably not exit your house and kill your neighbor's cat or your family members unless you are firing through a wall directly into a room occupied by them. These rifles also commonly have magazines with a very high capacity, which means you just flip the safety and pull the trigger until the threat is neutralized.

Shotguns The two types of shotguns are gas operated auto-loaders and pumps. Pumps are much more reliable than auto-loaders. The former will cause an incredible amount of havoc and devastation, but is more prone to failure. The latter is much more reliable, extremely cost-effective, and is still usable with very little training. Because these weapons have a very high muzzle energy, you will want to consider the occupants of your house if you pick this weapon. If you have many family members in the home, you will want to pick birdshot to avoid over-penetration. If it's just you and your spouse in the same room, you can generally go with 00 buckshot.

Regardless of what weapon you choose to defend your home, make sure you put a light on it. Positively identifying threats is crucial to avoid tragic mistakes, and with a good weapon light you get the secondary benefit of temporarily blinding your intruder.
